attributes.cardDescription: An external vendor, agency, or freelancer with contract dates, length, a performance rating, a structured rate card, agreement terms, and year-to-date spend
attributes.readMe:
# Vendor

## Summary
An external vendor/contractor with `serviceCategory`, `contractStart` (date), `contractLength` (DurationField), and `performanceRating` (ScoreField), plus contact details. v1.2 adds the commercial record: `rateCard` (containsMany `RateCardEntryField` — structured {role, hourlyRate} rows rather than a free-text blob, so rates can be queried and compared against `Contractor.billableRate`), `agreementTerms` (TextAreaField for payment schedule / notice / exclusivity), and `spendYtd` (NumberField, dollars year-to-date).

## Import
```ts
import { Vendor, RateCardEntryField } from './vendor';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As a contract record.** `contractStart` + `contractLength` feed
`contractFacts()`, which derives the projected end date, months remaining and a
lifecycle state (upcoming | active | expiring | expired). The state is
**derived, never stored**, so it cannot drift from the dates.

**2. As a renewal alarm.** Inside the six-month window the card says so in
words and pairs it with a colour, so a scan of the Offers/Dashboard surfaces
which contracts need a decision.

**3. As a supplier on a project and of contractors.** `Project.vendor` and
`Contractor.vendor` both link here; a vendor has no outbound links of its own,
which makes it the leaf of the whole graph. There is deliberately NO
`contractors` linksToMany back-edge — the tracker queries contractors by
vendor live, so the list can never go stale.

**3b. As the commercial reference.** The `rateCard` rows are what a staffing
conversation actually queries ("what does TalentBridge charge for a senior
QE?"), `agreementTerms` holds the negotiated ground rules, and `spendYtd`
feeds budget review alongside the renewal alarm.

**4. As a performance record.** `performanceRating` (ScoreField) renders as
★★★★☆ **plus** the numeral, so the value survives greyscale.

**5. As the cheapest fitted upgrade in the app.** Every field is `contains` —
zero links — so its fitted view can show anything without a single
denormalized field. It is the reference case for a rich fitted tile.

## Template Usage
Embedded view is a facts grid; fitted is an icon + name + category row. The isolated view adds a Rate card panel (structured role → $/hr rows), an Agreement terms panel, and Spend YTD in the contract facts — each with an honest empty state when the vendor has no commercial record yet (see `Vendor/paylock-payroll`).

**Non-goals:** contracts and invoicing (the commerce kit owns those — `spendYtd` is a recorded figure, not a computed ledger roll-up); vendor onboarding workflow; rate-card enforcement (nothing blocks a Contractor whose billableRate exceeds the card — the data is there to compare, the judgement is human).
